log.why: Testing top candidate dnaK (0.403 prior) offers high information gain and can confirm it in one plate.
Treating at 10 µM splits Ticket 2's prior probability nearly in half (0.546 vs 0.454) while Ticket 1 incubates.
E8 splits the posterior mass evenly (0.510 for fliC/katG vs 0.490 for others) for maximum information gain.
Testing 30 µM splits the remaining posterior mass nearly in half and strongly confirms 30 µM if positive.
Ticket 1 has the least time left, and knocking out rpoB directly tests the leading hypothesis (0.439) against hisG (0.334).
Testing 100 µM separates the two remaining plausible thresholds, 100 µM (0.560) and 300 µM (0.334), before publishing.
Ticket 1 has only 31s left and hisG is at 0.550, so testing hisG directly can confirm or refute it before publishing.
Test half of Ticket 3's prior probability mass ({fliC, rpoB, ompF} = 0.520) using a free incubator while Ticket 1's E1 finishes.
With 14 seconds left, another experiment cannot finish in time, and 100 uM holds a strong 0.797 posterior.
With 22 s left on Ticket 3, testing gyrA maximizes single-plate accuracy between top candidates hisG and gyrA before publishing.
E9 splits Ticket 4's prior near 50% (0.539) and separates top candidates ftsZ and katG while we await Ticket 3's E2.
Testing metJ resolves the main rival to katG before Ticket 4 expires, raising expected accuracy above 81%.
E3 splits Ticket 5's prior nearly in half (0.452 vs 0.548) while finishing bench work before Ticket 4's E3 reads in 6s.
E4 splits the top hypothesis 10 µM (0.40 cumulative) from higher doses, maximizing expected posterior gain before round end.
With 14 s left, a new experiment cannot finish before publishing; wait 6 s for E4 to improve posterior above 0.320, then publish.
With 3 seconds left in the round, no experiment can finish, and publishing 30 µM at 0.435 posterior has positive expected value.
